Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma
 Oral Order

Though this matter is listed for admission, with the consent of both the parties, the same is taken up for final hearing and disposed off by this order.
2.

The petitioner, being the sole accused in Crime No. 30/2022 of the then ACB, now Lokayuktha,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 13(1)(a) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, is seeking to quash the criminal proceedings registered against him.

3. Brief facts of the case are that :
Respondent registered the first information in Crime No.30/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 13(1)(a) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,
against the petitioner alleging that he is working as Executive Engineer in B.D.A and misusing his authority as such by permitting the former owners of Sy. No. 26/1 NC:
2024:KHC:44046 measuring 16 guntas of land to illegally trespass over the same by collecting development fees and issuing No Objection, even though the land in question was acquired several years back by the BDA and the owners have obtained compensation.
The petitioner has permitted the former owners to illegally trespass over the property and to squat over the same by accepting illegal gratification.

Therefore, the police registered the case and investigated into the matter.
4.
Heard Sri Jeevan K, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Suresh G.M, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Sri B.B.Patil, learned counsel for respondent.
Perused the materials on record.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner started working as Executive Engineer in the BDA, even according to the informant, from 27.09.2018.
The acquisition of the land was much before, the issuance of No Objection Certificate was also earlier to he joining the duty.
Under such circumstances, no offence is made NC: 2024:KHC:44046 out against the petitioner.
Hence, he prays for allowing the petition.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent, opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.

Investigation will have Sri K Mahadeve Gowda vs The State Of Karnataka on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37359835/
2 to be undertaken by the investigation officer.

sentences.text: He prays for dismissal of the petition.

7. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioner has made out any grounds to allow the petition and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:44046 REASONS 8.
The informant has made very serious and specific allegations against the petitioner.
It is stated that the land in question was acquired by the BDA and the compensation was paid to the owners of the land.

However, subsequently the owners managed to obtain No Objection Certificate and paid the development charges in respect of 16 guntas of land illegally and the petitioner being the Executive Engineer is said to have accepted illegal gratification and permitted commission of the offence.
The allegations are very serious in nature.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that other officials working in BDA must have joined hands with the owners of the property cannot be a ground to quash the criminal proceedings.
Proper investigation by the investigation officer will reveal the truth in the matter.
If the petitioner is not the person who has committed the offence, definitely final report will be filed accordingly.

If in the meantime it is found by the investigating agency NC: 2024:KHC:44046 that several other persons are also involved in the case, nothing prevents the investigating agency to investigate and file the report against them.
But I am satisfied that there are prima facie materials against the petitioner for having committed the offence and hence a case for investigation by the investigating agency is made out.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for any of the relief claimed in the petition.

9. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
